name: fig_verdict_flow
title: How check outcomes become verdicts
question: How do the per-check outcomes produced by the Lean checker combine into the three verdicts over the real catalogue, and does every verdict follow the stated combination rule?
model: Combination rule of `verdict` in lean/CryoLean/Checker.lean: unconfirmed -> NEED_MORE_INFORMATION; any mandatory applicable fail -> DOES_NOT_MEET; all pass or not-applicable with at least one pass -> MET; otherwise NEED_MORE_INFORMATION. Outcomes are those of relevantReqs and relevantCoupled.
data: Two Lean check_batch runs over all 286 experiment x configuration pairs (11 experiments x 26 configurations), confirmed and unconfirmed; 1118 mandatory applicable checks. Script paper/scripts/fig_formal.py; data paper/data/fig_verdict_flow.json; verdicts agree with paper/data/e1_grid.json for 286/286 pairs.
caption: (a) Every mandatory, applicable check outcome produced by the Lean checker over the 286-pair grid, routed to the verdict of its pair (band width = number of checks). (b) The same pairs grouped by the branch of the `verdict` definition they reach, plus the same pairs with unconfirmed profiles. All 572 Lean verdicts match the branch, and confirmed verdicts are 20 MET, 157 NEED INFO and 109 NOT MET; 240 of the checks inside NOT MET pairs are themselves unknown, because one trusted failure suffices to reject. Verdicts and outcomes are computed by Lean; the rule is the definition proven correct by verdict_accept_iff and verdict_reject_sound/complete.
